title: Postmortem: Cross-region reroute loop caused by variant-to-region policy mismatch
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:12 UTC, a subset of traffic began experiencing elevated error rates and timeouts across multiple regions. The control-plane smart-routing policy attempted cross-region reroutes to satisfy latency and capacity constraints but entered a reroute loop when fallback selection chose a model variant incompatible with the target region's instance class. This created a loop of reroute decisions and queue growth, resulting in degraded latency for affected customers and several 5xx spikes. Impact: ~2.3% of production requests experienced >2x latency and ~0.6% returned 5xx during the 28-minute window. Root cause: a recent policy change (policy engine commit 9a3f4a) introduced variant preference ordering that did not include region-capability checks for a small subset of experimental variants. When a primary routing target was unavailable, the fallback engine selected a variant that the target region could not start quickly (due to GPU type mismatch), which caused automated cross-region rerouting to try alternate regions that in turn rerouted back, forming a loop. Detection: automated SLO alerts (latency and 5xx rate) triggered; on-call flagged repeated reroute decisions in router logs and dashboard spike on "routing.loop.count" metric. Immediate mitigation: engineering disabled the new variant preference rule and enforced a temporary hard stop on cross-region reroutes for the affected customer tier; traffic was then drained and latency recovered.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC - first SLO alert (p95 latency) for region-us-west-2
2026-03-10 03:15 UTC - on-call (Diego) begins investigation; finds repeated reroute entries in router audit logs
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - disabled variant preference rule (policy rollback) and paused cross-region reroutes for standard tier
2026-03-10 03:28 UTC - error rates and latency begin returning to baseline
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC - incident declared resolved; follow-up work scoped for postmortem
root_cause: Policy engine allowed fallback selection of experimental variant without verifying regional instance compatibility
No guardrail/circuit-breaker for repeated cross-region reroutes in router logic
Insufficient unit/integration tests covering variant-to-region compatibility and fallback behavior
Change to policy ordering (commit 9a3f4a) lacked targeted rollout and runtime validation
short_term_mitigations_done: Paused cross-region reroutes for affected customer tiers and re-routed traffic to local compatible variants
Added an alert on "routing.loop.count" and increased sampling of router audit logs
Performed a manual reconciliation of variant-to-region capability table
long_term_action_items: A1: Add region-compatibility checks to fallback selector (owner: Diego Morales) — due 2026-03-21
A2: Implement reroute circuit-breaker that prevents >3 successive cross-region reroutes per request (owner: Priya Anand) — due 2026-03-28
A3: Extend policy engine CI with integration tests that simulate variant startup failures and validate fallback outcomes (owner: Martin Kline) — due 2026-04-04
A4: Add pre-deploy policy lint step that fails on preference rules referencing variants not flagged 'region-compatible' (owner: Lina Zhou) — due 2026-03-25
A5: Build a daily reconciliation job and add a console dashboard showing variant->region capability matrix (owner: Observability team) — due 2026-04-11
A6: Run a tabletop incident drill with routing and dedicated teams to exercise fallback and rollback playbooks (owner: Diego Morales) — due 2026-04-08
